newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND AND SYKORA GO FOR MORE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND AND SYKORA GO FOR MORE.

text.p: In a class of their own since the season started, downhill star Luc Alphand and slalom expert Thomas Sykora will pursue more glory in two races tailored to their measurements at the weekend.

Saturday's downhill and Sunday's slalom in the French Alpine resort of Chamonix, which will count for the season's first men's combined event, will give them fine opportunities to underline their supremacy ahead of the world championships next month in Sestriere, Italy.
Frenchman Alphand, who has already won two races in Val Gardena and Bormio, would love to score a win on home snow in this picturesque ski resort overlooked by Mont Blanc.
Austrian Sykora, who has won three of the four slaloms staged so far and finished second in the other, looks almost unbeatable at the moment.
"The way I'm skiing right now is just unbelievable," he said. "It looks like I can make mistakes and still win a race. But I know it will not last for ever."
Alphand sounded a clear warning to his rivals by clocking the fastest time in Wednesday's first downhill practice with the other contenders all more than a second behind.

"There's not much we can do against him at the moment," sighed world champion Patrick Ortlieb after finishing well behind. "I hate to say it but he's the best of us," added the Austrian, not exactly Alphand's best friend.

Unlike Ortlieb, Frenchman Adrien Duvillard gets on well with Alphand. The two men share a room on the circuit. They also use the same skis, which seem to be the ultimate weapon on the Chamonix piste as Duvillard was the fastest in Thursday's practice.
Not very steep, the piste is made tricky by spectacular bumps on its upper part and nasty bends through a pine forest.
The lower part, which finishes in the hamlet of Les Houches just outside Chamonix, will be used for the slalom, which brings back sweet memories for World Cup holder Sebastien Amiez of France.

"It's here that I earned my first top 10 placing," recalled the Frenchman, who came sixth when the World Cup last stopped in Chamonix in 1994. "I've never won in France and I would love to", added Amiez, who was second to Sykora last Monday in Kranjska Gora, Slovenia.
Others to watch in the slalom will be Norway's Tom Stiansen, who won the only slalom which eluded Sykora last December in Breckenridge, Colorado, and consistent Austrian Thomas Stangassinger.

It would not be wise to rule out flamboyant Italian Alberto Tomba, far from his best in his recent outings but eager to boost his morale ahead of Sestriere, where he dreams of shining before his adoring fans.

Tomba, who halted training in Italy on Wednesday after a flare-up of pain in the wrist he injured in a fall last October, came to Chamonix and intends to take part in Sunday's race but will not make a final decision before Saturday, a spokeswoman for his ski manufacturers said.
The forecast predicts miserable weather with poor visibility for both races but it takes more than clouds to tame such formidable competitors as Alphand and Sykora.
